sampling_model.design: Independent observations from \(P_Q\), with a deterministic three-way sample split and known uniform covariate design on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with conditional ignorability and \(\kappa\le\pi_Q(x)\le1-\kappa\).
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform overlap is fixed over \(\mathcal X\); the full class also has a positive density band around \(x_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Private tensor-spline sufficient-statistic releases for \(\pi_Q\) and \(\mu_{0,Q}\), followed by Hölder-ball projection; a separate block supplies the privatized linear and quadratic local moments.
sampling_model.privacy: Replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differential privacy under parallel composition across disjoint blocks, a single joint Gaussian release within each block, and post-processing for stabilization and interval formation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The higher-order local-polynomial learner attains the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate under its regularity conditions.
Worst-case bias-aware local-polynomial confidence intervals are honest and shrink at the optimal nonparametric rate.
A doubly robust uniform confidence band is constructed for a lower-dimensional CATE function under nonprivate sampling.
DP-CATE preserves Neyman orthogonality asymptotically and gives quasi-oracle conditions for private two-stage CATE learners.
Theorem 4.6 constructs a valid private interval for the population ATE from private point and variance estimates.
A black-box resampling framework converts a private estimator into an asymptotically valid and tight nonparametric confidence interval.

body.tldr: The paper constructs a replacement-private, finite-sample honest interval for pointwise CATE on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the uniform-design attainable submodel. Projected private spline pilots, a clipped higher-order local moment, joint Gaussian releases, and spectral stabilization yield coverage for every finite higher-order dimension subject to the bandwidth domain and the local effective-sample condition. Deterministic tuning achieves the phase-sensitive length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\); this is a construction-specific upper bound, not a full-class minimax frontier. On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), the proved information is only the ordinary lower bound and the trivial length-two upper bound, so the exact private confidence modulus remains open.

project_justification.gap: Private CATE papers provide point releases or quasi-oracle guarantees, and private causal interval papers treat regular average effects. They do not give a uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage theorem that accounts simultaneously for higher-order nuisance bias, sampling uncertainty, privacy composition, and privacy noise.
project_justification.niche: A bias-aware fixed-length construction on a fixed KBRW-attainable positive-density submodel permits honest nonregular causal inference without assuming the desired coverage or length and without relying on the rejected paired-microcell lower bound.
project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment, proves unrestricted-finite-rank concentration, a uniform finite-sample remainder inequality, honest coverage, and the phase-sensitive expected-length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\) for the concrete attainable class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\). Separately, it proves the ordinary regression lower limitation on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\). The attainable construction is not transferred to the full class: under the lower theorem's conditions \(L_\pi\ge1/2\) and \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), the strongest honest statement there is the bracket \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le2\), with exact sharpness unresolved.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) establish the privacy-free pointwise CATE rate and motivate the higher-order local-polynomial architecture. Their upper theorem requires its stated design-density and population-Gram conditions; this paper verifies the needed identities only for its uniform-design attainable construction and does not assert that the KBRW upper transfers to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\). Nor is KBRW's density-hole fuzzy lower asserted to transfer to the present full class with a positive anchor density band. Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the quadratic correction. Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias. Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) provide nonprivate doubly robust CATE bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) study private orthogonal CATE learning but do not derive this pointwise Hölder coverage and length phase; Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) treat private intervals for the regular population ATE. Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give an asymptotic resampling conversion for private estimators, whereas the present construction supplies uniform finite-sample bias control. Dwork and Roth (2014) provide the Gaussian mechanism, parallel composition, and post-processing facts used by the accountant.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The displayed higher-order privacy term comes from the global sensitivity \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+k h^{-2d})\) of a direct clipped quadratic-moment release. It is an attainable upper-bound cost, not a minimax lower bound. The proposal does not revive the invalid \(q<\gamma\) paired-microcell transport construction and does not claim that this term is unavoidable on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).
body.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy of the explicit learner and interval, uniform finite-sample coverage on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the attainable-class achieved length upper \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\), the corrected construction-specific privacy-free reduction with no rank floor, and the ordinary full-class lower limitation. The attainable class is restricted to uniform design and is generally a strict submodel whenever the declared density band admits nonuniform designs; no attainable upper bound is transferred to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\). Under \(L_\pi\ge1/2\) and \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), only \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le2\) is settled for the full class. Whether that bracket is tight, including whether a nuisance-driven privacy branch is unavoidable, remains the open-ended question.
